title: Redwood Year-End All-Hands
next_steps: Share Q4 results deck and recording (slides link: https://redwood.internal/q4-deck)
Send security & compliance pack (SOC2/ISO summary + KMS integration note)
People team to share org changes and hiring guidance by 2026-12-23
action_items: Owner: Priya Singh — Circulate org changes and hiring guidance — Due: 2026-12-23
Owner: Maya Chen — Publish Q1 roadmap doc + prioritization notes — Due: 2027-01-07
Owner: Rafael Gomez — Share service reliability post-mortem summary and capacity plan — Due: 2026-12-30
Owner: Ethan Cole — Compile top 10 customer asks we saw in Q4 and GTM asks — Due: 2027-01-05
summary: Year-end all-hands with CEO and leadership covering Q4 highlights, business metrics, product roadmap priorities for Q1, and company-wide org/compill changes. Emphasis on production reliability, Dedicated traction, and private deployments. Short Q&A and next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Asha Patel: Okay everyone, thanks for joining the year-end all-hands. Well get started. Its 10am PT on Dec 20th. Were running about 75 minutes. Hello team.
[00:12] Crowd noise / applause / clapping; some people joining late.
[00:25] Asha Patel: Quick housekeeping — recording is on, transcript will be shared. Weve got leadership updates, product highlight, and then Q&A. Ill run through the company high-level and then Luca will do tech, Maya product, Rafael infra, Priya will do people.
[00:40] Asha Patel: First, thank you. Big thanks — the end of year energy has been amazing. Q4 overall we saw strong usage growth in Hosted API, and Dedicated customer renewals came in above our plan. Two notable enterprise wins in November — banking and healthcare — both required private deployments and SOC2/ISO touchpoints which our security team handled.
[01:05] Asha Patel: High level numbers — ARR growth quarter over quarter was high 20s percent, net dollar retention held around 112% (this is rough, we’ll put the exacts in the Q4 deck). We continue to be mindful of unit economics; Redwood Optimize has helped a handful of large customers reduce token spend via caching and smart batching.
[01:28] Asha Patel: We did see a handful of outages in October that impacted latency. We’re prioritizing reliability next quarter, which means additional SRE headcount and infra investment. Rafael will talk specifics.
[01:40] Asha Patel: On the go-to-market side, we’ve tightened our pricing tiers for Hosted vs Dedicated to better communicate tradeoffs on latency and cost. Ethan will share more with Sales.
[01:52] Asha Patel: On runway and finances — we closed a modest top-up earlier in the year and are in a healthy position, but we are being conservative on hiring in H1; there will be targeted hires in eng and product for reliability and core infra. People team will share details.
[02:10] Asha Patel: Any questions on the high-level stuff before we hand over?
[02:15] [silence / murmur]
[02:20] Luca Romano: Thanks Asha. Quick tech update. We shipped the new KV cache eviction policy in early December; initial benchmarks show about 15% lower average latency for seq lengths under 1024 for chat workloads when cache hit rates are above 60%. These are early numbers. There’s also work on kernel selection for quantized weights which helps on Ampere and new H100-class machines.
[02:48] Luca Romano: We’re seeing the usual hazards in inference — long-tail requests, cold cache churn, and some inefficient batching patterns from SDK users. We’re shipping more SDK sampling controls to help teams tune batching and cache hints.
[03:04] Speaker 3 (Rafael?): Uh Luca, could you say more about the Dedicated autoscaling changes?
[03:09] Luca Romano: Yeah, good callout. We changed the default burst policy so Dedicated pools have a small reserved slot for sudden bursts that keeps p99 latency bounded while still respecting commit capacity. It does increase cost slightly in some configs. Rafael will share the cost models.
[03:25] Maya Chen: Quick product update: We’ve prioritized three bets for Q1: 1) Reliability and latency SLOs (observability + auto-fallback policies), 2) Private deployment maturity (easier VPC + on-prem packaging), and 3) Developer UX for tool calling and structured outputs in the Redwood API. We’re consolidating a roadmap doc and will open a public-ish internal RFC for feedback next week.
[03:51] Maya Chen: On the model catalog side, we’ve added two community models and one Redwood-verified variant with improved quantization profiles. We’re still balancing quality regressions; please flag anything you see.
[04:04] Audience: applause / emoji reactions
[04:10] Rafael Gomez: Infra and reliability: we added two more GPU clusters for Dedicated in EU-west and pushed a few kernel-level optimizations. Post-mortem for the October incident is done — root cause was a KV cache race under specific eviction patterns with long-lived sessions. The mitigation is rolled, but long-term we’re changing how we shard caches and will add stronger chaos testing. Expect a capacity and SLO runbook by 12/30.
[04:38] Rafael Gomez: Regarding Private deployments — we’re streamlining the customer install so it’s less ops-heavy. We’ve been doing pilot installs for two customers and learning about KMS/HSM integration pain points. We will publish a KMS integration guide in the security pack.
[04:55] Priya Singh: People update — first, thank you again for the work this year. We’re doing a small organizational restructuring in Platform and some hiring slowdowns elsewhere. No layoffs — the changes are to align priorities and free up runway for SRE and infra investments. We will have individual manager syncs starting Monday. Compensation review timeline will be communicated next week.
[05:18] Priya Singh: Also holiday closure — office will be limited from Dec 24 to Jan 2. On-call is still covered per schedule.
[05:28] Ethan Cole: GTM highlights — top 10 Enterprise asks this quarter were private deployment, SLA-backed latency, better billing visibility, SSO/SAML and RBAC controls, and more model options for embed/rerank tasks. We’ve prioritized a security packet to address the first 4 items in sales cycles.
[05:52] Ethan Cole: Renewal rate for Dedicated customers was strong; some movement to multi-year contracts. We’ve also seen more RFPs citing SOC2 and ISO-27001 which is driving our compliance playbook.
[06:05] Asha Patel: Okay, Q&A time. Please put questions in chat or raise your hand.
[06:12] [Q&A begins]
[06:15] Speaker 7 (Sarah - Eng): For Rafael — whats the timeline for the SLO runbook and extra SRE hires?
[06:21] Rafael Gomez: Runbook by 12/30, hiring reqs — we’re opening two senior SRE roles this quarter, interviews start mid-Jan.
[06:28] Speaker 8 (Tom - Product): On model catalog regression, Maya can you comment on how we’re rolling back?
[06:33] Maya Chen: We’re using canary rollouts and have a quick rollback flag. If quality dips we switch traffic to a variant or previous version; we’re also expanding evals on our end-to-end prompt sets.
[06:45] Speaker 9 (Finance - Julia): Asha any guidance on comp budgets for next year?
[06:50] Asha Patel: We’re holding comp pools steady for critical hires. Broader comp increases will be considered after we see Q1 performance against reliability goals. Details from People next week.
[06:59] Speaker 10 (New Hire - Ben): Quick question on private deployment licensing — will pricing be different for on-prem vs VPC?
[07:05] Ethan Cole: Yes Ben, on-prem tends to be an enterprise licensed model with a larger platform fee; VPC private is more standardized but we price for support and host-level costs. We’ll circulate a pricing FAQ.
[07:16] [brief crosstalk re: holiday plans]
[07:22] Speaker 11 (Ops - Leah): Are there any changes to incident post-mortem transparency?
[07:27] Rafael Gomez: We will keep post-mortems internal but summarize action items and system changes to the company; absolute root cause details that are sensitive to customers will be redacted. We want more transparency on what changed.
[07:40] Speaker 12 (Legal - Ana): Quick compliance note — we’re finalizing ISO paperwork with auditors, should close in Q1. SOC2 readiness is stable; we’ll post a short FAQ for sales.
[07:53] Asha Patel: Thanks Ana. Okay, closing remarks — 2026 was a year of scaling our product-market fit. The next year is about making the platform dependable and refining where we win: production economics and enterprise readiness. Please read the Q4 deck when it lands and give feedback on the roadmap RFC.
[08:15] Asha Patel: I’m proud of the team. Rest over the holidays, and we’ll come back focused. Any final questions?
[08:25] [silence / reactions]
[08:30] Asha Patel: All right, meeting adjourned. Recording and transcript will be posted. Recap in chat with links and action items. Happy holidays.
[08:40] End of recording.
